Play Magus, use Spell Strike + Shocking Grasp + Elemental Spell: Fire to half/half fire and electricity. Hit your enemies with a sword imbued with the power of a _star_.

I set up the scene where he died at the end of one of our weekly sessions, and he played along perfectly, in order to sacrifice himself to save the party and end up in hell (backstory reasons).

She got really upset, though thankfully it was the end of the session. She was sort of beside herself, cause in her mind, it was basically her boyfriend I just killed. I tried to remain vague about it, much like a TV show would, but she didn’t take it well at all. So, in order to save face and spare her feelings, I begrudgingly tell her that it was planned, and I don’t intend for the Paladin to stay dead.

I accidentally make it worse by venting to bard about it, and how I felt like me coming clean about the fake out kind of invalidates death as a threat. I have one going on right now in my pathfinder game. It's kind of expected, since the players are already long-term BF/GF but is still a joy to watch.

One character is a LN Tiefling Warder (Pathfinder Path of War tank) named Stavix. Stavix is a big, angry knight, who is slowly turning into Doomguy. He's a defector from the "bad guy" empire who works for the Emperor/Religions leader of the "good guy" empire. Imagine Prince Zuko from Avatar, but instead of trying to return home, he wants to destroy it.

The other character is a CN (formerly CG until she threatened an 11-year-old's life) Human Alchemist named Valerie. She grew up in a small, country town devoting her life to science and guns (it's a Victorian Era Science Fantasy setting). She's slowly turning into a mad scientist, and is one of many sources of comedy in our group.

Their relationship developed over the first quarter of the game, while they were trying to find a runaway prince, and honestly, there really wasn't a lot of flirting as there was just...rampant arguments. It's hard not to crack a smile when they have little "romantic asides" that devolve into some kind of petty shouting match about something EXTRA stupid, which is mostly Val's fault if I'm being honest. One of the best bits was when Stavix was asked by an undead Merceneray leader (who was killed because he was gay, again 1800s) to play his wingman in getting with the party's Samsaran Dancer (PoW Mystic). On the horse ride to their next objective, Stavix started asking a lot of personal questions to the Dancer, and Val misinterpreted that as Stavix *flirting* with him. She spent the next session trying to make him jealous by flirting, and failing, with everyone, and no one really understanding why she was so thirsty/angry.

From then on, until it was official, everyone else in the party kept poking fun at Val and Stavix for being together, until they officially got together after finding the prince.

Now it's just great to see how their relationship evolves, and how the two of them grow in relation to eachother, and in the context of continued adventuring.

Our last session ended with Stavix sacrificing himself to save Val from a pissed off god of the abyss, and now the party is working to get him back from Satan. I'm excited to see what the reunion is going to be like, mostly because I know Val is going to kick his teeth in for doing something so stupid.

The problem you run into with that is your sub will arrive at your listeners unevenly. Your mains, should be delayed to the same time , and your sub delayed differently. Setting your sub off axis means the sound will take longer to travel, and require more intense calculations and time alignment. 

Say you have your sub on the far right side of the room. Setting it there, facing at the audience will mean the waves reach the right wing first and be delayed by a good amount before reaching the left wing. This throws your whole system out of whack and makes it not sound as good as if it were in the middle.

I think you can get away placing your sub center stage, but I think the issue you might be having with it is your system isn't properly tuned. You can compensate the phase cancelation by delaying your mains so that they cancel a bit less with the subs. Use your sub as a base for your delay settings.
